en.title: Lanterns Trailer Drops Manhunters, Sinestro, and a Galaxy-Spanning DC Threat
en.summary: The upcoming HBO Max series **Lanterns** has finally offered a substantial glimpse into its cosmic scope, revealing formidable foes and iconic villains. This new trailer promises a much grander narrative than initially anticipated, drawing in fans with its escalating stakes.
en.body:
The wait is over: **Lanterns**, the highly anticipated DC series for HBO Max, has just unleashed a trailer that pulls back the cosmic curtain, revealing a universe far more perilous than previously imagined. While earlier glimpses offered hints of the strained mentorship between veteran **Hal Jordan** (Kyle Chandler) and the eager **John Stewart** (Aaron Pierre), this latest preview explodes with the introduction of the **Manhunters** and the chilling presence of **Sinestro**. These aren't just minor skirmishes; the trailer positions the Manhunters as "the most dangerous beings to ever exist in the galaxy," immediately elevating the series' threat level.

The narrative core, which centers on Jordan and Stewart investigating mysterious murders in a small town alongside a skeptical local detective (Kelly Macdonald), now appears to be the tip of a much larger iceberg. The introduction of the Manhunters, the ancient robotic enforcers who predated the Green Lantern Corps, suggests a story that will delve deep into the history and foundational conflicts of the Lantern universe. This isn't just about policing space; it's about confronting an existential threat with roots stretching back eons. The trailer showcases the awe-inspiring – and sometimes adorable – applications of Green Lantern power, but it’s the looming shadow of the Manhunters and the iconic villain Sinestro that truly underscore the immense scale of the story being told.

## A Cosmic Reckoning

For fans who might have felt the Green Lantern mythos was too niche or complex, this trailer serves as a powerful invitation. The focus on a galaxy-wide threat and the inclusion of universally recognized DC villains like Sinestro broaden the appeal significantly. It signals that **Lanterns** is aiming for a sweeping, epic narrative that resonates beyond the core readership, promising a visually stunning and thematically rich exploration of duty, power, and the consequences of cosmic policing. The tension between Hal’s weary experience and John’s burgeoning idealism is now set against a backdrop of unimaginable danger, making their partnership, and the fate of the universe, feel incredibly high-stakes.

## What's Next

With the premiere drawing closer, the **Lanterns** trailer has ignited fervent discussion across fan communities. The reveal of the Manhunters and the clear escalation of the narrative arc have fans speculating about which other iconic Lantern lore elements might be incorporated. The series is set to premiere on HBO Max in the coming weeks, and this trailer suggests that viewers are in for a sprawling, character-driven cosmic epic that could redefine the Green Lanterns for a new generation.

By Molly Templeton | Published on July 27, 2026 Image: John Johnson/HBO Max Comment 0 Share New Share Lanterns Trailer Reveals Manhunters, Sinestro, and a Much Bigger DC Story Than Expected&url= target=”_blank” title=”Twitter”> Lanterns Trailer Reveals Manhunters, Sinestro, and a Much Bigger DC Story Than Expected” target=”_blank” title=”Pinterest”> Image: John Johnson/HBO Max With only a few weeks until the premiere of Lanterns , the powers that be at DC Studios have decided to—finally!—reveal a little more about what goes down in the upcoming HBO Max series. The new trailer has a few bits recycled from previous trailers, but for the most part it pulls the curtain way, way back. Manhunters! Sinestro! Adorable uses of Green Lantern powers! And a much bigger sense of the scale and threat of this extremely appealing series! I feel quite confident in saying that Lanterns has a lot going for it, even if you have not, historically, cared much about Green Lanterns. The basic shape of Lanterns has been clear for a while: Elder Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) is, very reluctantly, training upstart Lantern John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), who is chafing a bit at having to work under grumpy old Hal. They go to a small town to investigate some suspicious murders, and they have to work with skeptical cop Kelly Macdonald. What has only now become clear is that this is a (Martian) Manhunter situation. Manhunters are described in the trailer as “the most dangerous beings to ever exist in the galaxy,” and we see at least one, from behind, as he (?) grows into his actual shape. Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion) turns up to tell Hal, “He’s gonna send an army to put you down,” though it is not at all clear who “he” is, in this sentence. And Hal goes to visit his old mentor-turned-villain, Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen), who somehow knows about Hal’s new mentee. Who is not really Hal’s understudy. “He’s my replacement,” a grumpy Hal admits. Attendees at San Diego Comic Con got to see a lot more than the trailer, as several clips were shown to the Hall H crowd. io9 has a good rundown , should you want the spoilers, and The Direct added a key detail about Laura Linney’s mysterious role : She’s playing one of the Guardians of the Universe, the ancient founders of the Green Lantern Corps. All of these details are catnip for comics fans, but the trailer is also just plain good , even if you aren’t steeped in the lore. Chandler and Pierre play beautifully off each other, surly and resentful and reluctantly admiring in turn, and there are some fun bits and some dramatic bits involving their magic ring powers (they had me with the bottle opener).
